name: a2uiverse
description: The A2UIVerse extension (SPEC §14): the platform's one A2A extension. Between orchestrator and client, the metadata contract for cross-agent UI composition. A canvas is an A2A context: an utterance that opens one carries no contextId, the orchestrator mints it, and every later message in the canvas carries it. Outbound, the composition stamp (provenance, role) on every relayed event, the paintMeta part naming a paint ahead of its createSurface — the orchestrator's own for the layout surface, carrying the Planner's title for the canvas — and the synthesis payload — the derived data model of formula leaves, its match claims, and the sort declarations of a merged view — on the event that paints a synthesis surface; inbound, the parent canvas on the utterance that opens a child, and the composition operation — the reader's press on the composition: Retry, Include, Try again, a fragment's step back, a scope request dismissed, the canvas closed — on a message of its own. From an agent, read and never required, the auth-required request in A2A's own requirement shape. Nothing a2uiverse-specific rides the vendor wire. Normative for every language projection; each projection's contract test asserts against this file.

sourceId.rule: A source is the app and the account it paints under. <n> is a short ordinal the AuthVault assigns per app at that account's first sign-in and never reuses; a slot for an app that needs sign-in, while the vault holds no account for it, is named for the account its sign-in will create — the next ordinal. A source with no account — an app whose card needs no sign-in, and shell — is the bare app id. The id carries neither the account's label nor its subject. App ids never contain the separator.

surfaceIdNamespacing.rule: The orchestrator namespaces surfaceId on the four A2UI server→client message types and reverses it on inbound client actions. Component ids, binding paths, and catalog ids are never rewritten.

compositionStamp.carriedOn: every relayed A2A event's metadata, keyed by stampKey

fields.source: Provenance and placement: the source id the event came from — the app and the account it painted under. A fragment's surface fills the layout's Slot whose source is this id.
fields.role: Which surface the canvas renders as the composition root: 'shell' | 'fragment'.
fields.vendorContextId: Debug only, gated by orchestrator config.
fields.vendorTaskId: Debug only, gated by orchestrator config.
fields.settled: This source's stream has ended: set on one event the orchestrator emits after relaying a fragment source's last event, with no A2UI parts. The client judges that source's fragments there instead of at the turn's end.

canvasParent.carriedOn: the opening utterance's message metadata, keyed by stampKey — the key is two-directional: the stamp outbound, the parent inbound; absent on a root canvas

fields.parent: The contextId of the canvas this question was asked from: the trail's edge, and the canvas the Planner reads as this canvas, its ancestry as the recent turns.

clientSession.carriedOn: every client message's metadata, keyed by stampKey, beside the parent on an opening utterance

fields.session: The client's page load: minted once when the page loads and named on every message it sends, so the orchestrator can keep what holds for one sitting — whether an app's full sign-in tile was shown (task-12.5 decision 6). A reload is a new session.

compositionOperation.carriedOn: a data part of its own, {version, operation}, on a new A2A message in the canvas's context — beside the A2UI action, the error report and the utterance; version is the A2UI version the client speaks

fields.kind: The press: 'retry' sends again what one source's slot keeps — the action inside the fragment that failed or needed a scope, otherwise the slot's request from the plan — and is also the resume after sign-in, the orchestrator checking the vault again first; 'include' folds the sources that arrived after the merge into it; 'tryAgain' makes again a merge whose call failed; 'step' reports a fragment stepped back or forward in its own history — the paint's data model rides a2uiClientDataModel as on an action; 'dismiss' is Not now on a scope request: the press that needed the scope is dropped and the request taken off the attribution; 'close' ends the canvas: everything running in it cancelled, its composition dropped.
fields.sources: The source ids the press names: exactly one with 'retry', 'step' and 'dismiss', at least one with 'include', none with 'tryAgain' and 'close'.
fields.step: With 'step' only, required there: the paint id the fragment now shows — one paint per createSurface from that agent, counted the same way on both sides, from 0, never reused. A non-negative integer.

catalogLoadFailure.carriedOn: A2UI's client error report — a data part {version, error} on a new A2A message in the canvas's context — under the protocol's generic error, its code catalogLoadFailedCode; the protocol's error admits the extra field

fields.surfaceId: The fragment's surface, namespaced as the hub sent it: the slot it fills fails.
fields.message: The client's reason the catalog did not load, for the journal: the registry unreachable, the catalog not in its table, an interface version the client does not provide, the exports, the id, the entry throwing.
fields.catalogId: The catalog the client could not load: the slot fails with cause 'load', carrying it.

paintMeta.carriedOn: a data part of its own, {paintMeta: {...}} with no version field, its part metadata mimeType paintMetaMimeType, emitted ahead of the createSurface it names; the A2UI extractor never takes it

fields.surfaceId: The surface the paint creates, as the client will see it — namespaced for a fragment, shell:main for the layout surface.
fields.title: A short title for the paint, at most paintMetaTitleMaxLength characters. On the layout surface it is the Planner's title for the canvas, naming its entry in the trail; a longer one is clipped with an ellipsis by the orchestrator and journaled, never a plan finding; absent, the client falls back to the question. On a fragment it is the agent's own title for the paint, naming it in the fragment's history.
fields.kind: The paint's declared kind: 'question' marks a surface the canvas routes to its overlay slot.

paintMeta.authors: The orchestrator emits the part for its own layout surface. A vendor agent's part is the agent kit's, in this same shape, relayed untouched; the contract describes the part, it does not own the kit's emission — an agent that never emits one composes, its paints titled from their cause.

authRequired.carriedOn: a data part of the status message of a task in A2A's `auth-required` state, recognized by the state and its `security` key; no A2UIVerse marker

fields.security: What the agent needs, in the card's own `security` requirement shape: a list of alternatives, at least one, each mapping a scheme key on the card to the scope keys in that scheme's `scopes` map it is missing. An empty scope list asks for a sign-in with that scheme. A key the installed card does not declare makes the request invalid.

authRequired.authors: An agent that needs authority mid-task — scope escalation — moves its task to `auth-required` with this part, as A2A's in-task authentication describes (A2A 0.3 §4.5). The agent kit emits it for the platform's own agents; any other agent may, in the same plain A2A vocabulary. The contract describes the part, it does not own an agent's emission; an agent that never emits one is read as its card declares.

synthesizeDataModel.carriedOn: metadata.a2uiverseSynthesis of the event that paints a synthesis surface; the tree is painted as ordinary A2UI on the same event
synthesizeDataModel.authors: The orchestrator's Synthesizer writes the merged view; the orchestrator validates it, paints its tree in the shell catalog, and sends the derived data model and the sorts as the synthesis payload.

synthesis.title: SynthesisPayload
synthesis.description: Client-facing: the synthesis branch minus the tree (painted as A2UI) and the note (journaled). Evaluated client-side into the synthesis surface's data model.

ref.description: A cross-partition qualified ref: a pointer that resolves in another surface's data model.

surface.description: The namespaced surfaceId (<source>:<surfaceId>) the pointer resolves in.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into that surface's data model, where a segment may carry a predicate: `items[sku="x"]` selects the element of `items` whose field `sku` equals the JSON literal "x", and `items[a="x",b=2]` conjoins several field tests until exactly one element matches. Elements are selected by key, never by position: a positional segment into an array does not resolve. A ref is valid while its keys resolve; none matching and several matching are both absent. The value is a JSON literal compared by JSON equality.

formula.description: A leaf of the derived model: one operator over N refs, N ≥ 0. A plain vendor value is a one-argument pass-through. A formula with no refs is a value no source contributes to — absent by construction. Operators are names the shell catalog declares as functions; the contract does not enumerate them. Recognized by shape: an object with exactly `op` and `args` is a formula.

op.description: A function name declared by the shell catalog.

relation.description: One named relation of a match claim: a formula like any other leaf, its operator a relation the shell catalog declares, over exactly two refs in two different sources — the source of each ref's namespaced surface — so two accounts of one app can be joined, and a source never to itself. The contract does not enumerate relations; the consumer checks the operator against the shell catalog.

op.description: A relation the shell catalog declares as a function.

match.description: A match claim, under the reserved key `match` of an object of the derived model, the root included: the Synthesizer's word that the entries the object joins from different sources are one thing, with its evidence. Each key is the Synthesizer's own words for what matched, each value a relation. At least one relation; flat. No object is required to carry one. Disclosed on the object's values by the shell's derived-value component; the tree binds no path under `match`.

node.description: A node of the free-form derived model: a formula leaf, an object whose values are nodes — its key `match`, when present, is its match claim — or an array of nodes. A scalar anywhere is a violation — every leaf is a formula, never a literal value.

dataModel.description: The derived data model the tree binds to: a JSON shape of the Synthesizer's choosing whose every leaf is a formula. Evaluated client-side into plain values with contributor state at the same paths. The key `match` on any object, the root included, is that object's match claim. The root key `sorts` is reserved: the runtime writes each sort declaration, with the user's current choice, at `/sorts/N` of the synthesis surface's data model, and the tree binds SortControl there.

sort.description: A sort declaration over one array of the derived model, or — through `*` — over the list inside every element of the arrays enclosing it, all of them ordered alike. The model names the array, the sortable keys and their labels, and the initial choice; the runtime sorts and keeps the user's choice of key or direction, one choice for every list the declaration reaches.

path.description: JSON Pointer to the sorted array in the derived model. Its steps are object keys and `*`: a `*` passes through every element of an array, at any depth, so `/rows/*/runs` names the list `runs` inside every element of `rows`. Every element the path passes through carries the list, `[]` when it has none. The last step names the array; an array is never stepped into by position, and no step selects an element by key.

options.description: The keys the user may sort by, each with its user-facing label.

key.description: JSON Pointer inside each element of the sorted array — of every list the path reaches — to a formula leaf.
The initial key; one of the options.

canvasIdentity.rule: Each canvas is its own A2A context. The utterance that opens a canvas is sent with no contextId; the orchestrator mints one and the client reads it from the first event. Every later message in the canvas — action, press, error report — carries it. The orchestrator holds one composition per context for the session; a vendor's context is per canvas.
